name: Adam and Eve
charge: Hearkening to the serpent’s doctrine, that ye shall not surely die; and eating the fruit of lies
summary: Adam was the chosen man, formed of the dust of the ground outside the garden and set inside it, and given the breath of life, which is the commandments. The serpent is Satan the deceiver, who played on the woman’s envy and taught her a doctrine: that she would not die, and that her eyes would be opened and she would be as gods. She ate the lie and taught it to her husband. Their nakedness was sin, and the sin was idolatry; the fig leaves were a covering of transgression, and the trees they hid among were the other people in the garden. Judgment fell on the serpent, the woman and the man; God covered them with the first sacrifice and drove them out, and set a flaming sword turning every way to keep the way back.
offenseFull: Adam was the chosen of the Most High. Out of all the people created on the earth he had a favourite from the beginning: he formed him of the dust of the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and that breath is the commandments (Genesis 2:7; 2 Esdras 3:5; Proverbs 7:2). He was formed of the soil, and the richer the soil the darker. He was formed outside the garden and then placed inside it, eastward in Eden, where the river Gihon compassed Ethiopia (Genesis 2:8-14). No help meet was found for him among the women already on the earth, which is more proof the earth was peopled beyond that house, so the woman was made of his rib (Genesis 2:18-23). He was set there with one commandment concerning the tree, and some of those trees are literal trees while some represent men (Genesis 2:16-17; Mark 8:24).

The serpent is not a snake; serpents do not speak. Another word for serpent is deceiver, and the serpent is Satan, who transforms himself into an angel of light (Genesis 3:1; 2 Corinthians 11:14). Satan taught her doctrine and played on the words: she had been taught that breaking the commandment meant death, and he told her she would not die at all, but that her eyes would be opened and she would be as gods (Genesis 3:4-5). What he worked on was envy, for through envy of the devil came death into the world; there was one God in that house and she wanted to be equal with her husband (Wisdom of Solomon 2:24). Good for food is good to learn, and the fruit she ate was the lie; she taught her husband what the serpent taught her, and he broke the commandment also (Genesis 3:6; Hosea 10:13). The first attack in the scriptures is on a household, and it began with the woman: of the woman came the beginning of sin (Ecclesiasticus 25:24). Adam’s charge is that he listened to his wife’s voice against the command given him (Genesis 3:17).
judgmentFull: They were not literally naked. Nakedness is sin, and the sin is named elsewhere: when Aaron made the calf, Moses saw the people naked, for Aaron had made them naked to their shame among their enemies, and the worshipping of idols is the beginning, the cause and the end of all evil (Genesis 3:7; Exodus 32:25; Wisdom of Solomon 14:12, 27). The fig leaves are Adam covering his transgressions and hiding his iniquity within himself (Job 31:33; Lamentations 1:8). They hid among the trees of the garden, and the trees are people: they tried to hide their sin among the others in the garden with them, and no cedar in the garden of God could hide him (Genesis 3:8; Ezekiel 31:8). The question of where he was was a call to self-examination. Adam blamed the woman, and in saying she was given him blamed the Most High also; then Eve blamed the serpent (Genesis 3:9-13).

The serpent was cursed above all cattle and above every beast of the field, and the cattle and the beasts are the nations. Going on the belly and eating dust is a very low estate, a vagabond upon the earth, and the prophets say the nations will lick the dust like a serpent (Genesis 3:14; Micah 7:16-17; Isaiah 49:23). Verse fifteen is prophecy. The woman is the nation of Israel; the enmity between Satan’s seed and her seed remains; the bruised heel is Israel made to stumble, and the bruised head is Christ destroying the works of Satan under the feet of his people (Genesis 3:15; Jeremiah 3:2; Romans 16:20). To the woman it was said that her desire would be to her husband and that he would rule over her: her desire had been to learn from the serpent, and she was sent back to learn from her husband, one of the first commandments given (Genesis 3:16; 1 Corinthians 14:34). To Adam the ground was cursed, with sorrow and sweat all his days, and death was appointed in him and in his generations, of whom came nations and tribes out of number (Genesis 3:17-19; 2 Esdras 3:7-8).

The coats of skins were the first sacrifice, ordaining the sacrificial law: a beast slain to clothe them and cover their sin, and that lamb, slain from the foundation of the world, is Christ (Genesis 3:21; Leviticus 16:27; Isaiah 61:10; Revelation 13:8). Then the man was driven out to till the ground he was taken from, and cherubims and a flaming sword turning every way were set at the east of the garden to keep the way of the tree of life; a sword turning every way is confusion, so the way back could not be found (Genesis 3:22-24).

lawsResolved.text: I am the LORD your God, you shall have no other gods besides me.
You shall not make for yourself any carved image, or any likeness of anything; you shall not bow down to them nor serve them.

text.text: And the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
And the Lord God planted a garden eastward in Eden; and there he put the man whom he had formed.

And out of the ground made the Lord God to grow every tree that is pleasant to the sight and good for food; the tree of life also in the midst of the garden, and the tree of knowledge of good and evil.
And a river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from thence it was parted, and became into four heads.
The name of the first is Pison: that is it which compasseth the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold;
And the gold of that land is good: there is bdellium and the onyx stone.
And the name of the second river is Gihon: the same is it that compasseth the whole land of Ethiopia.
And the name of the third river is Hiddekel: that is it which goeth toward the east of Assyria. And the fourth river is Euphrates.
And the Lord God commanded the man, saying, Of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat:
But of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die.
And the Lord God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.

And out of the ground the Lord God formed every beast of the field, and every fowl of the air; and brought them unto Adam to see what he would call them: and whatsoever Adam called every living creature, that was the name thereof.
And Adam gave names to all cattle, and to the fowl of the air, and to every beast of the field; but for Adam there was not found an help meet for him.
And the Lord God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof;
And the rib, which the Lord God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man.
And Adam said, This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man.
And gavest a body unto Adam without soul, which was the workmanship of thine hands, and didst breathe into him the breath of life, and he was made living before thee.
Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye.
And he looked up, and said, I see men as trees, walking.
Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the Lord God had made. And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?
And the woman said unto the serpent, We may eat of the fruit of the trees of the garden:
But of the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of the garden, God hath said, Ye shall not eat of it, neither shall ye touch it, lest ye die.
And the serpent said unto the woman, Ye shall not surely die:
For God doth know that in the day ye eat thereof, then your eyes shall be opened, and ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.

And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise, she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.
And no marvel; for Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light.
Nevertheless through envy of the devil came death into the world: and they that do hold of his side do find it.
Ye have plowed wickedness, ye have reaped iniquity; ye have eaten the fruit of lies: because thou didst trust in thy way, in the multitude of thy mighty men.
Of the woman came the beginning of sin, and through her we all die.
And when Moses saw that the people were naked; (for Aaron had made them naked unto their shame among their enemies:)
For the devising of idols was the beginning of spiritual fornication, and the invention of them the corruption of life.
If I covered my transgressions as Adam, by hiding mine iniquity in my bosom:
Jerusalem hath grievously sinned; therefore she is removed: all that honoured her despise her, because they have seen her nakedness: yea, she sigheth, and turneth backward.

The cedars in the garden of God could not hide him: the fir trees were not like his boughs, and the chesnut trees were not like his branches; nor any tree in the garden of God was like unto him in his beauty.
The nations shall see and be confounded at all their might: they shall lay their hand upon their mouth, their ears shall be deaf.
They shall lick the dust like a serpent, they shall move out of their holes like worms of the earth: they shall be afraid of the Lord our God, and shall fear because of thee.

And kings shall be thy nursing fathers, and their queens thy nursing mothers: they shall bow down to thee with their face toward the earth, and lick up the dust of thy feet; and thou shalt know that I am the Lord: for they shall not be ashamed that wait for me.
I said in mine heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.

Lift up thine eyes unto the high places, and see where thou hast not been lien with. In the ways hast thou sat for them, as the Arabian in the wilderness; and thou hast polluted the land with thy whoredoms and with thy wickedness.
And the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen.
Let your women keep silence in the churches: for it is not permitted unto them to speak; but they are commanded to be under obedience, as also saith the law.

And unto him thou gavest commandment to love thy way: which he transgressed, and immediately thou appointedst death in him and in his generations, of whom came nations, tribes, people, and kindreds, out of number.
And every people walked after their own will, and did wonderful things before thee, and despised thy commandments.

And the bullock for the sin offering, and the goat for the sin offering, whose blood was brought in to make atonement in the holy place, shall one carry forth without the camp; and they shall burn in the fire their skins, and their flesh, and their dung.

I will greatly rejoice in the Lord, my soul shall be joyful in my God; for he hath clothed me with the garments of salvation, he hath covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decketh himself with ornaments, and as a bride adorneth herself with her jewels.
And all that dwell upon the earth shall worship him, whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.
